# Data

The Washington Statistical Analysis Center is a clearinghouse for state data on crime and justice topics, brought together from many different agencies and reporting systems. Use our Web-based query tools to target your crime and justice questions and search the databases for answers. Full data sets from each database are downloadable in Excel or SAS for more detailed analysis.

## Criminal Justice Data Book

The Washington State Criminal Justice Data Book combines state data from multiple agency sources that can be queried through CrimeStats Online.

* [The Criminal Justice Data Book (CJDB): The CJDB Overview Infographic](https://sac.ofm.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/CJDB_Overview_Infographic.png)

* [The Criminal Justice Data Book (CJDB): An Overview of the CJDB](/sites/default/files/CJDB_Overview.pdf "CJDB_Overview.pdf")  
   The purpose of this report is to provide an overview of the CJDB including its role in integrating criminal justice data across the justice system, improving public access through CrimeStats Online, supporting research and evidence-based policymaking, addressing important data considerations, and identifying opportunities for future development.

* [The Criminal Justice Data Book (CJDB): The Data Dictionary](/sites/default/files/cjdb_dictionary.pdf "cjdb_dictionary.pdf")  
   The purpose of this report is to serve as a data dictionary for the CJDB, providing background information about each subject area, including data sources, collection methods, statistical definitions, and important caveats to support accurate interpretation of the data.

* [The Criminal Justice Data Book (CJDB): The Reference Guide](/sites/default/files/CJDB_Reference_Guide.pdf "CJDB_Reference_Guide.pdf")  
   The purpose of this report is to serve as a reference guide for the CJDB by documenting each dataset and topic, identifying its data source, explaining what it measures, and providing important notes regarding definitions, methodology, and interpretation.

* [The Criminal Justice Data Book (CJDB): The Database Architecture](/sites/default/files/CJDB_Architecture.pdf "CJDB_Architecture.pdf")  
   The purpose of this report is to provide a comprehensive overview of the CJDB system’s architecture, including the integration of data from multiple criminal justice agencies, the relationship between the CJDB and the Justice Data Warehouse (JDW), and the governance and quality assurance practices that ensure the accuracy, consistency, and reliability of statewide criminal justice reporting.

### CrimeStats Online contains data on:

* reported crimes
* adult and juvenile arrests, sentences, and dispositions
* superior court filings
* prison admissions
* prison populations

[CrimeStats Online](/crimestats-online "CrimeStats Online")

* [Data 1985–1995](/washington-state-county-criminal-justice-data-book-1985-1995 "Washington State County Criminal Justice Data Book: 1985 to 1995")

## Justice Data Warehouse

The Justice Data Warehouse (JDW) is an integrated criminal justice data platform that connects and analyzes data from Washington State’s courts, corrections, law enforcement, and related justice agencies to provide a comprehensive view of justice system involvement and support data-driven decision-making. It is intended to support research efforts and help agencies analyze trends, improve decision-making, and coordinate activities across courts, law enforcement, and corrections systems. By providing secure and standardized access to information, it promotes transparency, accountability, and evidence-based policy development.

* [The Justice Data Warehouse: The JDW Overview Infographic](https://sac.ofm.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/JDW_Overview_Infographic.JPG)  
   The JDW Overview Infographic provides a visual summary of the data available within the system and how it can be used to better understand trends and patterns in the justice system.
  
* [The Justice Data Warehouse: The JDW Process Infographic](https://sac.ofm.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/JDW_Process_Infographic.JPG)  
   The JDW Process Infographic provides an overview of how justice-related data are collected, processed, integrated, and made available through the Justice Data Warehouse. It illustrates the key steps involved in transforming source data into information that can support analysis and decision-making.
  
* [The Justice Data Warehouse: The JDW Handbook Infographic](https://sac.ofm.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/JDW_Handbook_Infographic.JPG)  
   The JDW Handbook Infographic provides an overview of the Justice Data Warehouse handbook and its guidance for understanding and using JDW data. It highlights key information about the data, processes, and resources available to support consistent and informed use of the warehouse.
  
* [The Justice Data Warehouse: The JDW Data Governance and Data Security Infographic](https://sac.ofm.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/JDW_DG_and_DS_Infographic.JPG)  
   The JDW Data Governance and Data Security Infographic provides an overview of the policies and practices used to manage, protect, and maintain justice-related data within the warehouse. It highlights the importance of data quality, privacy, security, and appropriate access to ensure responsible use of JDW data.
  
* [The Justice Data Warehouse: The Data Handbook](https://sac.ofm.wa.gov/sites/default/files/SJS_JDW_Handbook.pdf)  
   The purpose of this report is to establish the Justice Data Warehouse (JDW). This integrated platform links criminal justice data from the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC), Caseload Forecast Council (CFC), Department of Corrections (DOC), Washington State Patrol (WSP), and Washington Association of Sheriffs and Police Chiefs (WASPC), offering a comprehensive, longitudinal view of individuals’ justice system involvement. The JDW enhances transparency, supports data-driven policy, and enables collaboration across criminal justice agencies. It empowers stakeholders to identify system gaps, evaluate reforms, and design more equitable and effective justice system strategies. By centralizing criminal justice data and supporting Tribal and local jurisdictions, the JDW plays a pivotal role in building a smarter, fairer, and more accountable justice system for Washington State.
  
* [The Justice Data Warehouse: Data Governance and Data Security](https://sac.ofm.wa.gov/sites/default/files/JDW_Data_Governance_Data_Security.pdf)  
   The purpose of this report is to describe the data governance structure and the data security for the JDW. Through rigorous governance and review procedures, the JDW mitigates the adverse effects of poor data quality, promotes responsible and secure data management, enhances transparency, and supports data-driven policy and cross-sector collaboration. By centralizing justice data while safeguarding privacy and supporting state and local jurisdictions, the JDW plays a pivotal role in building a smarter, fairer, and more accountable justice system for Washington state.
  
* [The Justice Data Warehouse: COVID-19 Metrics and Indicators](/sites/default/files/justice_data_warehouse_and_covid.pdf "justice_data_warehouse_and_covid.pdf")  
   The global 2020 coronavirus pandemic has had an unprecedented impact on the operations and actions of local, state, and national governments across all areas of criminal justice. The unique characteristics of this pandemic trend toward short- and long-term consequences as significant changes to criminal justice and legal outcomes. To respond to these impacts, the Washington Statistical Analysis Center (SAC) applied for and received the 2022 State Justice Statistics (SJS) grant from the Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS). The SAC sought the grant to increase access to statistical data and create new metrics and indicators to enhance the integrated criminal justice database — the Justice Data Warehouse (JDW) — in efforts to strategically and analytically evaluate the pandemic’s impacts in criminal justice. Through this grant, the Washington SAC leveraged and built upon the JDW to expand the data variables by creating COVID-19 metrics and indicators to help assess and account for COVID-19 impacts in the criminal justice and legal system.

## Uniform Crime Reporting

Summary Reporting System (SRS) and the National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) are part of [the FBI's Uniform Crime Reporting system](https://www.fbi.gov/about-us/cjis/ucr/ucr). SRS and NIBRS collect data on crime incidents that are reported by law enforcement agencies across the country. Because SRS and NIBRS data are collected differently, they cannot be compared.

### Summary Reporting System

SRS has been used since the 1930s to collect national crime data. Washington SRS data is available from 1994 to 2018. Data will no longer be produced from the SRS as of 2018.
